jurisdiction.venue: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) & Federal Reserve / OCC / FDIC / NCUA

docket_number: FinCEN Order FIN-2026-R002 & Federal Reserve SR 26-10
headline: America’s Anti-Money-Laundering Watchdog Went Offline — and Handed Wall Street a 42-Day Filing Holiday
deck: Weeks after fining Bank of America $1.21 billion over late suspicious activity reports, FinCEN’s own batch-transfer channel suffered a service disruption, prompting four banking regulators to waive citations until Dec. 30 and point urgent tips to a 1-866 phone line.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: FinCEN Order FIN-2026-R002 (Nov. 24) and Joint Statement SR 26-10 by the Federal Reserve, FDIC, OCC, and NCUA (Nov. 25) paused Bank Secrecy Act and Beneficial Ownership Information batch-filing deadlines from Nov. 18 through Dec. 29 until Dec. 30, 2026, waiving enforcement for affected SDTM filers during FinCEN’s service disruption.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Spending a decade fining drivers for missing toll-transponder pings, then shutting down the highway toll server for six weeks and asking anyone witnessing a bank heist to call an 866 hotline
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Zero supervisory citations for batch-filing banks through Dec. 30, contrasted with automatic statutory penalties when ordinary taxpayers miss a filing window

interactive_art_spec.caption: The United States Treasury Building in Washington at dusk. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network granted 42 days of temporary exceptive relief for batch Bank Secrecy Act filings disrupted by a Secure Data Transfer Mode outage.
